item.title: Tru Phonic — Sun Jul 26, 2:00 PM — Meadow at Highland Brewing Co.
item.description:
Bio
The original music of Jake Salter & a unique group of talented musicians come together in Tru Phonic. Sounds of Jam, Funk, Blues, Rock, Soul, Jazz and Hip-Hop & more can be heard when seeing the band Live or on their Studio Albums. Established in 2017, Tru Phonic includes Multiple veterans in the Central Florida music scene who have worked with many other great bands and musicians in the area. The group has an ever-changing, high-energy live show that makes you wanna MOVE! Tru Phonic’s original sound is characterized by high skill-level shown on each instrument, talented vocal harmonies, powerful lyrics, expanding grooves, unique guitar playing & a tight horn section. ​In just a few years of touring Tru Phonic has made quite an impression everywhere they go, establishing fanbases & regular listeners in cities allover the Southeast U.S. & Booking Music Festivals Like Suwannee Hulaween 2023, Farm to Grass, Whippersnap Music & arts Fest, Sunshine Hootenany, Everglades Roots Fest

item.title: Canvass for Jeffrey Burroughs for City Council — Sun Jul 26, 11:45 AM — Asheville
item.description:

item.title: AT -From Sam's Gap South FITNESS HIKE — Wed Jul 29, 9:00 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group The Hike will start at the Sam's Gap parking lot. We will hike south on the AT for 5.75 miles to a view point. Snack there, then return. (11.5 miles out and back, approx. 2650 ft. elevation gain) the weather is looking fairly good at this point but maybe bring a raincoat just in case there is a shower. I will post any cancellation by 7:15 AM
**Pace:** We will hike at a brisk pace averaging approximately 2 1/2 -3 mph adjusting for steepness of grade and rugged trail conditions. Please be comfortable with this distance, elevation and pace. **Dogs; F**riendly dogs ok.
**Car Pool or Follow to the trailhead.** To Carpool, meet at the Park and Ride lot off Exit 17 on I-26 W at 8:30 am. Please post if you plan to meet us there otherwise we will see U at the trailhead at 8:50 am.
**Hike Levels:** Level (1) Up to 600 feet; Level (2) 600'- 900'; Level (3) 900' - 1200'; Level (4) 1200' - 1500'; Level (5) 1,500' - 1,800'; Level (6) 1,800' - 2,100'; Level (7) 2,100' -

item.title: Matt Smith’s Well-Crafted Music Series with Jon Stickley, Lyndsay Pruett and Christian Ferri — Wed Jul 29, 6:00 PM — Meadow at Highland Brewing Co.
item.description:
Matt Smith’s Well-Crafted Music Series The Well-Crafted Music Series is a weekly showcase curated by pedal steel guitarist Matt Smith, bringing standout talent to Asheville through fresh, genre-defying collaborations. Drawing from more than 20 years of touring and recording, the series highlights artists Matt has met and worked with along the way, creating one-of-a-kind performances you won’t see anywhere else. May – October, this series typically takes place on our scenic Meadow stage. During cooler months, Matt and friends will play in the Taproom. Chairs, blankets and well-behaved, leashed pets are welcome in the Meadow. Please note that coolers and outside alcohol are not permitted on the premises.
Source: Highland Brewing, Where Y'at AVL Music

item.title: My Generation — Fri Aug 14, 5:00 PM — Event Center at Highland Brewing Co.
item.description:
My Generation is a musical celebration of the songs that defined a generation. Bringing together three of Western North Carolina’s premier cover bands—Soul Blue, Vintage Vinyl, and Fringe Revival—this collaborative concert revisits the unforgettable sounds of the 1960s and 1970s, from psychedelic rock, folk, and pop to soul, R&B, funk, disco, and classic rock. Inspired by the powerful connection between music and memory, My Generation taps into the nostalgia of the era that shaped the Baby Boomer generation. Each band has carefully curated a set list that honors the artists, movements, and moments that transformed popular music and culture. Whether you’re reliving treasured memories or discovering these timeless songs for the first time, My Generation delivers an evening of exceptional musicianship, infectious energy, and the soundtrack of a remarkable era. Avoid the FOMO and go buy your tickets now! Get Tickets
Source: Highland Brewing, Where Y'at AVL Music

item.title: Fun & easy way to play more tennis (please read event description for details) — Tue Aug 18, 7:00 PM
item.description:
PlayYourCourt Asheville Tennis We’re still working to get more people into these Meetups, but our goal is to give PlayYourCourt members a few social tennis outings each week in addition to your practice sessions and Challenge League matches.
These Meetups are co-ed, super laid back, and all skill levels are welcome. Post your skill level and a suggested court in the comments section so we can round up as many players as we can for some tennis fun!
Also, if you’re looking to meet new practice partners or play some matches and you aren’t already in the PlayYourCourt Community, you can go here to see what we’re all about and sign up:
https://www.playyourcourt.com/tennis-community/asheville-nc/meetup/
If you love tennis, we’d love to have you! Be sure and watch the quick video that explains how everything works.
Happy hitting!
- Scott

item.title: The Art of Presence: Meditation and Reflection in the Museum — Sat Aug 22, 9:30 AM — Asheville Art Museum
item.description: Step into the Museum’s galleries before the doors open for a quiet and contemplative morning of meditation, mindful walking, and reflection. This guided experience invites participants to slow down, settle the nervous system, and explore the Museum as a place of sanctuary, spaciousness, and renewal. The session will begin with a brief seated meditation, followed by a walking meditation through selected exhibits. Along the way, participants will pause with gentle mindfulness prompts designed to support personal reflection, embodied awareness, and a deeper connection with the artwork. Rather than offering art historical interpretation, the experience encourages each participant to notice what arises within them through presence, stillness, and mindful seeing. The group will honor noble silence throughout much of the session with occasional opportunities for brief reflection and sharing. No previous meditation experience is needed. item.description:
Prepare for an unforgettable evening as Meschiya Lake and the Mood Swingers make their debut at Jack of the Wood on August 24th, 2024! From 9pm to midnight, experience the soulful sounds of this celebrated artist and her Asheville band. With a $10 cover charge at the door, don’t miss your chance to see Meschiya Lake live.
Newly based in Asheville, Meschiya Lake's journey began at age nine in South Dakota and took her from circus stages to the vibrant streets of New Orleans. Her powerful voice and dynamic performances have garnered accolades, including Female Performer of the Year at the Big Easy Awards and recognition from NPR.
Having toured globally, from Lincoln Center to stages across Europe and beyond, Meschiya Lake brings her unique blend of jazz and soul to Asheville. Join us at Jack of the Wood on August 24th for an evening of timeless melodies and captivating performances. item.title: NOBODY'S DARLING STRING BAND — Sat Sep 19, 4:00 PM
item.description:
Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.
Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.
The five women comprising Nobody’s Darling each have a long history of playing old-time music. Individually they have played in many other bands through the years, including The Carolina Oldtimers, The Pegtwisters, The Zuma House Band, Too Hot To Cook, The Luke Smathers Mountain Swing Band, Honey Holler, and The Carolina Chick Peas.
Stop in to enjoy the music and an afternoon libation or two, perhaps with an early supper or light bite . . . and don't forget your dancing shoes!

item.title: Weekly Critique — Wed Sep 30, 6:00 PM
item.description:
AVL Writers This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.
For our group discussion, please bring at least 8-10 printed copies of your piece. That way, we can all read through each other's work and provide feedback.
Sharing our creative efforts is an important part of the writing process. I'm really looking forward to reading what you've been working on. Don't worry if it's still a rough draft.
If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.
If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).
Source: AVL Writers
